function.name: calc_heat_capacity
function.description: Calculate the heat capacity at constant pressure of air using its temperature and volume. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

temp.description: The temperature of the gas in Kelvin.

volume.description: The volume of the gas in m^3.

gas.description: Type of gas, with air as default.

message.reasoning:
The user wants calculation of heat capacity at constant pressure (Cp) for air given T=298 K, V=10 m³. They didn't specify if they want per mole? Usually Cp depends only on composition not volume; but maybe use ideal gas law PV=nRT -> n=P*V/(R*T). But we don't have P. For standard conditions, assume atmospheric pressure ~101325 Pa. Then compute n. R=8.314 J/mol·K. So n = P*V / (R*T). Compute: P*V = 101325 * 10 = 1,013,250 Pa*m³ = Joules? Actually Pa*m³ = N/m² * m³ = Nm = J. Yes. Divide by (8.314*298)=2477.772 ≈ 2477.77. So n≈409 mol.

Heat capacity at constant pressure for dry air approx 29.1 J/mol*K. Multiply by n gives total C_p_total = 29.1 * 409 ≈ 11900 J/K. Let's calculate precisely: 29.1*409 = 11899.9 J/K.

Alternatively could give specific heat capacity per unit mass etc. Provide explanation.

We can also call function calc_heat_capacity? It expects temp, volume, optional gas. We might just provide answer manually. Use function? It's likely expecting us to use tool. We'll call it.
